rationale: The Latin anchors *fragorem edere* ("to make a crashing/cracking sound"), *sonare* ("to sound"), and *crepare* ("to creak/crack/make a sharp noise") all point firmly to an auditory sense — producing a sharp, explosive sound — rather than a physical fracturing sense. This aligns with crack.v.02 ("make a very sharp explosive sound"), consistent with the poetic contexts in Beowulf and Exodus where BERSTAN describes the loud noise of things bursting or crashing.
